topic.title: AI Evaluation, Governance, and Research Integrity
topic.overview: This topic examines how AI systems are assessed, maintained, and governed rather than proposing one predictive architecture. It includes benchmark credibility, independent safety research, technical debt, access, and human agency. Several representatives are position papers, so their recommendations should be understood as argued proposals rather than experimentally established solutions.
topic.whyItMatters: Evaluation incentives shape which systems appear successful and which risks remain invisible. Credible comparisons require attention to contamination, selective reporting, researcher access, and the operational context in which a model is used.
topic.evolution: The 2015 technical-debt paper emphasizes system dependencies and maintenance. Recent contributions propose safe harbors for independent evaluation, community-governed benchmarking, and preregistration for agent experiments. Newer studies also investigate saturation and coverage of social impacts. Together these works broaden assessment from isolated model scores to the institutions and practices producing them.
openQuestions: How can independent evaluation remain accessible without weakening test integrity?
Which reporting practices make changes in agent experiments auditable and reproducible?
